завершившись успешно. Независимое code review Sol medium и документационное
ревью завершились без замечаний. См. [Stage 2 report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36o--finite-binary-addition-and-subtraction-output-in-the-gap-64-profile).
В момент завершения S2-36o issue [ISSUE-024](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md#issue-024--s2-36-result-apis-lacked-large-gap-rounding)
оставалась открытой для exponent gap >64; S2-36 и hardware acceptance также
оставались открытыми.

#### S2-36p — finite binary addition and subtraction result APIs across the full finite exponent range

**Статус:** новые finite add/sub result APIs поддерживают весь конечный
диапазон показателей. Low-level exact-alignment и legacy convenience APIs
сохраняют контракт gap≤64. ISSUE-024 решена для полного result path; полная
приёмка S2-36 и hardware acceptance остаются открытыми.

Расширить только новые
`add_finite_aligned_result(lhs, rhs, mode)` и
`subtract_finite_aligned_result(lhs, rhs, mode)` для `Binary32`/`Binary64`:
все конечные нормализованные операнды поддерживаемых destination/source
сочетаний должны обрабатываться во всём диапазоне их конечных показателей.
Существующие low-level exact-alignment helpers и legacy APIs сохраняют
ограничение gap≤64 и текущие сигнатуры/поведение. Для gap≤64 сохранить
результаты и diagnostics S2-36o; при большем gap новые result APIs не должны
возвращать `None` только из-за величины gap.

Для нормализованных 64-bit significands `a` (старший по показателю), `b`
(младший), gap `d≥65`, и показателя старшего операнда `e` exact tail bridge
представляет результат как `(Q+T)·2^(E-63)`. После преобразования вычитания
в сумму эффективных слагаемых (rhs со знаком-копией, инвертированным для
subtraction), совпадающие знаки дают `Q=a`, `T=b/2^d`, `E=e`. Разные знаки
означают вычитание меньшей по модулю части из большей: при `a>2^63`
`Q=a-1`, `T=1-b/2^d`, `E=e`; при `a=2^63` `Q=u64::MAX`,
`T=1-b/2^(d-1)`, `E=e-1`. При `a,b∈[2^63,2^64)` и `d≥65` в первом случае
`0<b/2^d<1/2`, во втором `1/2<1-b/2^d<1`, а в третьем
`0<b/2^(d-1)<1`; следовательно, во всех трёх случаях `0<T<1` и `Q`
нормализовано. Большой gap не допускает cancellation.

Хвост проходит через приватный round-equivalent bridge, специализированный для
destination precision 24 и 53; bridge передаёт `r=1,d=4` как representative,
а не как точный quotient. Для нормального и subnormal округления число
отбрасываемых bits положительно, а целочисленная часть `Q` задаёт сторону
любого midpoint; ненулевой хвост отличает точный tie от значения выше/ниже.
Ветка subnormal `k=64` использует только факт ненулевого остатка, `k>64` —
только знак и ненулевость. Поэтому representative сохраняет итоговое значение
и diagnostics S2-36m для binary32/64, включая `tiny_after_precision_rounding`,
`overflow` и final `inexact`. Это не exact quotient и не общий bridge для
precision 64 или произвольного формата. Gap≤64 остаётся на точном `u128`
alignment path; low-level exact helpers и legacy APIs не изменены. Новые
dependencies, CPU flags, exception delivery, DAZ/FTZ, NaN/infinity и
instruction integration не добавлены.

Literal-векторы покрывают все rounding modes, оба знака и операции, gap
64/65/2097, significands `2^63`/`2^63+1`, midpoint sides, subnormal/min-normal
и overflow boundaries, результатные bits и diagnostics. Проверки автора
прошли: `cargo test -p od-isa --offline binary_float::tests` (48/48),
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline x87::tests` (47/47),
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, `git diff --check`, и
`graphify update .`. Graphify сообщил существующее предупреждение парсера для
`include/open_desktop/host_abi.h` и обновил граф успешно. Независимое code
review Sol medium и documentation review завершились без замечаний. ISSUE-024
решена для полного result path; low-level/legacy APIs сохраняют explicit
gap≤64 contract. Полная приёмка S2-36 и hardware acceptance остаются открытыми.
Форматный контекст binary32/64 — Intel SDM Rev.093, Vol.1
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)); формулы
`Q/T/E` являются проектной математикой, а не заявлением об instruction
semantics или hardware integration.

См. [отчёт S2-36p](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36p--finite-binary-addition-and-subtraction-result-apis-across-the-full-finite-exponent-range)
и закрытую [ISSUE-024](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md#issue-024--s2-36-result-apis-lacked-large-gap-rounding).

#### S2-36q — raw same-format binary32/binary64 addition and subtraction

**Статус:** raw add/sub result APIs реализованы; независимые code и docs
reviews Sol medium завершены чисто. Полная приёмка S2-36,
инструкция/exception integration и hardware acceptance остаются открытыми.

`Binary32::add_raw_result` / `subtract_raw_result` и соответствующие методы
`Binary64` принимают только два raw операнда одного destination формата и
возвращают `BinaryAddSubResult<Self>`: итоговое encoding, diagnostics
`inexact`, `overflow`, `tiny_after_precision_rounding` и отдельный
`invalid_operation`. Этот локальный boolean не является MXCSR/x87 status bit,
не решает exception masking и не доставляет исключение. Для raw finite
operands (zero, subnormal, normal) методы нормализуют только конечные поля и
делегируют S2-36p finite result APIs; поэтому сохраняются gap≤64 exact path,
large-gap bridge, exact-zero sign policy и signed zero при округлении
ненулевого конечного значения в ноль.

Для exact-zero суммы знак сохраняется при одинаковых signs effective zero
terms; противоположные signs дают `-0` только при `TowardNegative`, иначе `+0`.
Addition и subtraction используют знаки исходных terms после семантического
переворота RHS только для subtraction. Конечная ненулевая сумма сохраняет свой
точный sign, если округляется в zero.

Infinity handling возвращает signed infinity для определённых случаев.
`+∞ + -∞`, `-∞ + +∞`, `+∞ - +∞` и `-∞ - -∞` возвращают Intel QNaN
indefinite (`0xffc00000` для binary32, `0xfff8000000000000` для binary64) и
`invalid_operation=true`. Другие finite/infinity и infinity/infinity пары
сохраняют знак определённого бесконечного результата; invalid не выводится
из одного только присутствия infinity.

Для одного или двух NaNs выбирается первый source operand, который является
NaN. Выбранный QNaN возвращается без изменения; выбранный SNaN quiet-ится
установкой только quiet bit с сохранением sign/payload. Любой входящий SNaN
ставит локальный `invalid_operation`, даже если первым NaN был QNaN второго
типа; subtraction не переворачивает sign RHS NaN до propagation. Это правило
следует Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 1, §4.8.3.5 / Table 4-8 для source-order
NaN selection, а indefinite encodings — Vol. 1, Table D-1
([official Intel PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)).
Оно фиксирует локальную binary32/64 математическую операцию, не объявляя x87
source ordering, instruction dispatch или архитектурную exception delivery.

Literal-векторы для обеих ширин покрывают NaN source order, qNaN/sNaN,
preserved sign/payload, invalid infinity cancellation и signed-zero
combinations во всех четырёх rounding modes; конечные normal/subnormal/gap
cases сверяются с S2-36p diagnostics. Авторские проверки прошли:
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline binary_float::tests` (54/54),
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline x87::tests` (47/47),
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`,
`git diff --check` и `graphify update .` (успешно; Graphify сообщил notice об
изменении community labels). Независимые Sol medium code review и docs review
завершились без замечаний. Hardware/SSH проверка отложена до общего финального
substage; полная S2-36 приёмка остаётся открытой.

#### S2-36r — raw same-format binary32/binary64 multiplication

**Статус:** raw multiplication result APIs реализованы; независимые Sol medium
code review и docs review завершены чисто. Полная приёмка S2-36 и
hardware/Mac mini acceptance остаются открытыми.

`Binary32::multiply_raw_result` и `Binary64::multiply_raw_result` принимают
raw операнды одного формата и возвращают `BinaryArithmeticResult<Self>` с
encoding, diagnostics S2-36m и отдельным local `invalid_operation`. Старое имя
`BinaryAddSubResult` сохранено как public type alias, а сигнатуры add/sub API
остались совместимы. NaN обработка использует тот же first-source resolver,
что и S2-36q: выбранный QNaN сохраняется, выбранный SNaN quiet-ится только
quiet bit, любой SNaN помечает invalid. Источник — Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 1,
§4.8.3.5/Table 4-8 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)).

`0 × ∞` и `∞ × 0` возвращают отрицательный Intel QNaN indefinite для
соответствующего формата и `invalid_operation=true` (Table D-1 того же SDM).
Прочие infinity результаты имеют XOR sign; QNaN/SNaN propagation происходит
до проверки этих случаев. Конечные raw operands, включая zeros и subnormals,
нормализуются и делегируются `multiply_finite_result`, сохраняя single-rounding
и `inexact`/`overflow`/`tiny_after_precision_rounding`. Для special/invalid
результатов эти три rounding diagnostics false. Это локальный result contract,
не MXCSR/x87 status, masking или exception delivery.

Literal checks обеих ширин покрывают signs и operand order, QNaN/SNaN source
priority, `0 × ∞`, infinity combinations, finite×infinity, XOR signed zero по
всем rounding modes и finite exact/inexact/subnormal/underflow/overflow
delegation. Авторские проверки прошли:
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline binary_float::tests` (57/57),
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline x87::tests` (47/47),
`cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline`, `git diff --check` и
`graphify update .`. Independent Sol medium code review и docs review завершены
без замечаний; hardware/SSH и Mac mini проверка отложены до общего финального
substage. S2-36 не завершён.

#### S2-36s — raw same-format binary32/binary64 division

**Статус:** raw division result APIs реализованы; независимые Sol medium
code review и docs review завершены чисто. Полная приёмка S2-36 и
hardware/Mac mini acceptance остаются открытыми.

`Binary32::divide_raw_result` и `Binary64::divide_raw_result` принимают raw
операнды одного формата и возвращают отдельный `BinaryDivisionResult<Self>`:
result encoding, S2-36n rounding diagnostics, `invalid_operation` и
`divide_by_zero`. Это отдельный тип, чтобы не добавлять несвязанный divzero
outcome в общий arithmetic result. Все outcomes локальны и не обновляют
MXCSR/x87 state, не выполняют masking или exception delivery.

NaN propagation использует shared S2-36q/r first-source resolver до всех
special-case проверок: выбранный QNaN сохраняется, выбранный SNaN quiet-ится,
любой SNaN ставит invalid. Поэтому NaN над denominator zero не ставит
`divide_by_zero`. `0/0` и `∞/∞` дают negative Intel QNaN indefinite и
`invalid_operation=true`. Только finite nonzero divided by either signed zero
ставит `divide_by_zero`; `∞/0` возвращает signed infinity без этого исхода.
Остальные бесконечные случаи и zero/finite или finite/infinity дают знак через
XOR. Для всех special results три rounding diagnostics false. Finite/finite
включая zero numerator делегируют напрямую `divide_finite_result`, включая
zero sign, single rounding и S2-36n diagnostics.

Локальная классификация опирается на Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 1:
§4.9.1.3 (`#Z` только для finite nonzero/zero), §4.9.2 (QNaN precedes
divide-by-zero) и §4.8.3.7/Table D-1 (negative indefinite encodings;
[official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)). Эти правила
задают результат API, а не MXCSR/x87 status или исключение инструкции.

Literal tests обеих ширин покрывают zero/infinity/finite class combinations,
NaN/signaling NaN versus zero, signs и operand order, invalid versus local
divide-by-zero, нули во всех rounding modes и finite exact/inexact/subnormal/
underflow/overflow delegation. Авторские проверки: binary_float (60/60), x87
(47/47), fmt, workspace check, diff check и Graphify update. Независимые Sol
medium code review и docs review завершились без замечаний; аппаратная/Mac mini
проверка отложена до общего финального substage. S2-36 не завершён.

#### S2-36t — raw same-format binary32/binary64 comparison

**Статус:** raw comparison APIs реализованы; независимые Sol medium code review
и docs review завершены чисто. Полная S2-36 приёмка и hardware/Mac mini
acceptance остаются открытыми.

`Binary32::compare_raw` и `Binary64::compare_raw` принимают два raw операнда
одного формата и явный `BinaryComparisonMode::{Quiet, Signaling}`. Результат
`BinaryComparisonResult` содержит `BinaryComparisonRelation::{Less, Equal,
Greater, Unordered}` и отдельный local `invalid_operation`. NaN даёт
`Unordered` без quieting/rewriting: quiet mode отмечает invalid только для
SNaN, signaling mode — для QNaN и SNaN. Это compare predicate contract, не
first-source arithmetic NaN propagation. Infinities сортируются как signed
infinity; finite operands делегируют S2-36l `compare_finite`, включая
численное равенство `+0`/`-0` и subnormal/normal ordering. Raw `Eq` wrapper
сохранён; `PartialOrd`/`Ord`, EFLAGS, MXCSR/x87 state, instruction dispatch и
exception delivery не добавляются.

Нормативный контекст — Intel SDM Rev. 093, Vol. 2A: COMISD/UCOMISD §3-199,
COMISS/UCOMISS §3-201 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).
Для обеих инструкций NaN relation unordered; COMI signals invalid for QNaN or
SNaN, UCOMI только для SNaN. Этот raw API фиксирует relation/local invalid
без EFLAGS update или architectural delivery.

Literal tests обеих ширин охватывают qNaN/sNaN в обоих operand positions,
quiet/signaling mode, обе NaNs, неизменность raw bits, signed infinities/zeros,
subnormal/normal edges, adjacent normals и relation reversal. Авторские
проверки: binary_float (64/64), x87 (47/47), fmt, workspace check, diff check и
Graphify update. Независимые Sol medium code review и docs review завершились
без замечаний; аппаратная/Mac mini проверка отложена до общего финального
substage. S2-36 остаётся открытой.

#### S2-36u — raw binary32-to-binary64 widening

**Статус:** `Binary64::widen_from_binary32` реализован как exact raw-value
conversion; авторские локальные проверки и независимые Sol medium code/docs
reviews завершены чисто. S2-36 и hardware/Mac mini acceptance остаются
открытыми.

Метод принимает `Binary32` raw encoding и возвращает
`BinaryArithmeticResult<Binary64>` без rounding mode. Нули сохраняют sign;
normal и subnormal конечные значения точно расширяются integer-only путём;
все binary32 subnormals становятся normal binary64, включая минимум `2^-149`.
Infinity сохраняет class/sign. NaN сохраняет sign и source fraction, размещая
его в верхних 23 битах binary64 fraction; SNaN устанавливает target quiet bit
и сообщает local `invalid_operation`, QNaN его не сообщает. Все rounding
diagnostics false; метод не изменяет source, CPU/MXCSR state, не моделирует
denormal-input delivery и не выполняет instruction dispatch.

Нормативное преобразование NaN взято из Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 Table D-11;
CVTSS2SD Rev. 093 Vol. 2A §3-240 отмечен как будущий instruction consumer
([Vol. 1](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436),
[Vol. 2A](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). Эти ссылки
обосновывают raw conversion contract, не instruction admission, denormal
exception delivery или hardware evidence.

Literal vectors покрывают оба signs, zeros, normals, min/max subnormal,
all 23 subnormal leading-bit positions, minnormal/adjacent values, maxfinite,
infinities, QNaN/SNaN payloads and source immutability. Проверки прошли:
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline binary_float::tests` (67/67),
`cargo test -p od-isa --offline x87::tests` (47/47), fmt, workspace offline
check, diff check и Graphify update. Graphify успешно завершился с существующими
warnings для `include/open_desktop/host_abi.h` и files without symbols.
Независимые Sol medium code/docs reviews завершились без замечаний; hardware
acceptance отложена до общего финального substage.

#### S2-36v — raw binary64-to-binary32 narrowing

Implement `Binary32::narrow_from_binary64(source, mode)` as a value-only
conversion returning `BinaryArithmeticResult<Binary32>`. Preserve signed zero
and signed infinity. Convert every finite nonzero source from its exact
normalized binary64 significand through the binary32 target-precision/range
round-and-pack path exactly once; report inexact, overflow, and
tininess-after-precision-rounding diagnostics from that final conversion for
all four `RationalRoundingMode` values. Do not route through host `f32`/`f64`,
binary32 intermediate arithmetic, MXCSR, DAZ/FTZ, instruction dispatch, or
architectural exception delivery.

For NaNs, truncate the low 29 binary64 fraction bits and retain sign. A source
SNaN must set the binary32 quiet bit and return local `invalid_operation=true`;
a QNaN returns false. NaN conversion has no rounding diagnostics. Provenance:
Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 Table D-12 for NaN conversion and Vol. 2A
`CVTSD2SS` §3-234–235 for rounding control. Literal tests must include signed
zeros/infinities, payload truncation boundaries, exact finite encodings,
positive and negative tie cases, subnormal/tininess boundaries, and signed
overflow under all rounding modes. Keep full S2-36 and hardware/Mac mini
acceptance open; hardware execution is deferred to the combined final substage.

#### S2-36w — bounded signed i64-to-binary32/binary64 value conversion

Add `Binary32::from_i64(value: i64, mode)` and
`Binary64::from_i64(value: i64, mode)`, returning
`BinaryRoundingResult` for the corresponding format. Normalize the exact
unsigned magnitude without signed overflow (including `i64::MIN`), then call
the destination's existing `round_pack_quotient(sign, exponent, significand,
0, 1, mode)` exactly once. Zero is always positive zero. No i32-specific API is
needed; i32 values sign-extend through i64. Do not use host floating point,
binary64 as an intermediate for binary32, x87, CPU state, or MXCSR. Nonzero
results are normal finite values; `inexact` may be true, while overflow and
tininess are always false. In particular, `i64::MAX` may round to positive 2^63 without an
invalid or overflow outcome.

Use literal output encodings for zero, ±1, powers across every leading-bit
position, i32 limits, i64 limits and adjacent i64 values, and the integer
rounding boundaries around 2^24 and 2^53. Exercise both signs and all four
modes at ties and directed-rounding cases; include a binary32 literal above a
midpoint that would tie down after an intermediate binary64 rounding. Assert
literal bits and diagnostics; check normal class across each leading-bit case.
Intel SDM Rev.
093 Vol. 2A `CVTSI2SD` §3-236–237 and `CVTSI2SS` §3-238–239 specify signed
dword/qword conversion, MXCSR rounding control, and the SIMD Precision
exception. This pure helper accepts an explicit mode and does not mutate MXCSR
or deliver architectural exceptions. Full S2-36, instruction integration, and
hardware/Mac mini acceptance remain open; hardware execution stays deferred to
the combined final substage.

#### S2-36x — bounded raw binary32/binary64 to signed i32 conversion

Add `Binary32::to_i32(mode)` and `Binary64::to_i32(mode)` as local value-only
conversions returning `BinaryIntegerResult<i32>` with `value`, `inexact`, and
`invalid_operation`. Normalize finite raw encodings exactly, round to an integer
under the explicit mode, then validate the rounded value against the i32 range.
Both signed zeros convert exactly to zero. Non-finite sources or
rounded out-of-range values return the `i32::MIN` sentinel with
`invalid_operation=true` and `inexact=false`; exact `-2^31` remains valid.
The helper does not mutate the encoding, CPU state, or MXCSR and does not
deliver exceptions. Its invalid/inexact outcome is local and does not encode
architectural sticky flags or exception priority.

Literal checks cover both widths and all four modes, signed zero/subnormals,
halfway and adjacent encodings, ±1.5/±2.5, exact integers, exact i32 limits,
the binary64 quarter/half/three-quarter values around both range edges, binary32
adjacent range encodings, huge finite values, infinities, and both signs/classes
of NaN. Invalid results assert the sentinel and suppressed local inexactness;
all source encodings are checked unchanged. The exact local checks and current
limitations are recorded in the [S2-36x report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-36x--bounded-raw-binary32binary64-to-signed-i32-conversion).
Full S2-36/Stage 2 acceptance and hardware/Mac mini validation remain open.

Provenance: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSD2SI` pp. 3-232 and `CVTSS2SI`
p. 3-242 specify MXCSR rounding, range and masked indefinite behavior;
`CVTTSD2SI` p. 3-253 and `CVTTSS2SI` p. 3-255 specify truncation toward zero.
Vol. 1 §4.9.2 discusses invalid-exception precedence. These references do not
extend this helper into architectural exception handling.
[Official Intel Vol. 2A PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)
and [Vol. 1 PDF](https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/835781/325462-sdm-vol-1-2abcd-3abcd-4.pdf).

#### S2-36z — pure raw binary32/binary64 SSE MIN/MAX selection

Implement `Binary32::min_sse_raw_result`/`max_sse_raw_result` and the matching
`Binary64` methods as pure value selectors returning
`BinarySelectionResult<T>`, which contains only the selected raw value and a
local `invalid_operation` outcome. The SSE-specific method names distinguish
the right-operand selection behavior from IEEE minNumber/fmin operations.
Either quiet or signaling NaN selects the right operand unchanged and reports
invalid. For non-NaN operands, MIN selects the left operand only for strict
less-than and MAX only for strict greater-than; equality selects the right
operand, including opposite-signed zeros. Numeric comparison includes
subnormals without DAZ/FTZ. Do not report denormal exceptions, update MXCSR,
deliver architectural exceptions, or add instruction dispatch in this slice.

Literal tests cover lhs<rhs and lhs>rhs for both widths, subnormal order,
infinities, equal values, signed-zero ties in both operand orders, NaNs in
either position, multiple NaN payloads, unchanged signaling-NaN passthrough,
invalid outcomes for quiet/signaling NaNs, NaN noncommutativity, and source
immutability. Code review passed. The helper result APIs do not claim SSE
instruction integration, native/JIT behavior, MXCSR, exception delivery, or
physical-hardware acceptance.

Provenance: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MAXSS/MAXSD and MINSS/MINSD operation
definitions and SIMD floating-point exception tables. [Official Intel Vol. 2B
PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241).

#### S2-36aa — pure raw same-format binary32/binary64 square root

Implement `Binary32::sqrt_raw_result(mode)` and the matching `Binary64` method
as pure value operations returning `BinaryArithmeticResult<Self>`. Preserve
both signed zeros and positive infinity. Negative finite nonzero inputs and
negative infinity return the negative Intel indefinite QNaN and set local
`invalid_operation`; QNaN is returned unchanged, while SNaN is quieted by
setting its quiet bit and sets local invalid. This is a documented local
sign/payload-preserving policy, not a payload mapping inferred from Intel
Table 11-1. No source, CPU, MXCSR, or x87 state is changed, and no exception is
delivered.

For positive finite normalized `x = S * 2^(e-63)`, compute
`E=floor(e/2)`, `b=e-2E`, and `N=S << (63+b)`. An integer square-root helper
returns `q=floor(sqrt(N))`; verify `R=N-q²` using overflow-safe inequalities.
Pass quotient `q` to the existing same-format round-and-pack path with a
private representative tail of `0/1` when `R=0`, otherwise `1/2`. Document
that this tail is rounding-equivalent for precisions 24 and 53 (discarded
significand widths 40 and 11) and is not the exact fractional root remainder.
Use Euclidean/floor exponent division for negative `e`. Positive finite results
are normal and may report only `inexact`; the source can be subnormal.
Subnormal raw inputs are treated as their exact finite values. Reporting a
denormal-operand condition and DAZ/FTZ input handling are deferred; this pure
helper does not produce denormal diagnostics.

Tests include integer-square-root invariants for 0, 1, 2, perfect-square
neighbors, and `u128::MAX`; literal sqrt(2) and sqrt(0.5) encodings under all
modes for both formats; exact roots; subnormal and normal range boundaries;
special classes; diagnostics; and source immutability. Do not use host
floating-point square root or fabricated midpoint cases. Keep instruction
dispatch, x87, packed lanes, MXCSR, exception delivery, DAZ/FTZ, native/JIT,
and CPUID outside this slice.

Provenance: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 1 Table 11-1 identifies negative SQRT
inputs as invalid with QNaN indefinite response and refers SNaN handling to
Table D-10. This establishes the invalid/special-class context, not an exact
NaN sign or payload mapping for this local helper. Vol. 2B `SQRTSD` pp. 4-667–
4-668 and `SQRTSS` pp. 4-669–4-670 list invalid, precision, and denormal
exceptions. Architectural denormal reporting and MXCSR behavior remain outside
the helper contract. [Official Intel Vol. 1 PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436)
and [Vol. 2B PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241).

#### S2-36ab — deterministic raw binary32 SSE reciprocal reference

Add `Binary32::reciprocal_sse_raw()` as a pure deterministic reference for
legacy RCPSS/RCPPS value semantics. Signed zero and every signed subnormal
input map to same-sign infinity; infinity maps to same-sign zero (inferred from
`APPROXIMATE(1/SRC)`); QNaN is preserved and SNaN is quieted by setting the
quiet bit while preserving sign and payload. Normal finite inputs use the
existing exact same-format division for `1.0 / source`, rounded once using
fixed nearest-ties-even. A subnormal rounded result is flushed to same-sign
zero. There is no local diagnostics result, CPU/MXCSR mutation, exception
delivery, instruction dispatch, packed-lane support, DAZ/FTZ framework, native
or JIT behavior.

This is a deterministic local reference policy, not a claim about exact
hardware output bits. Correctly rounded normal outputs have relative error at
most `2^-24`, within Intel's `1.5 * 2^-12` bound. Tests use integer-only exact
significand products to check `|x*y - 1| <= 3/8192` for nonzero normal outputs;
flushed zeros are excluded. Coverage includes all subnormal leading-bit
positions, both signs and zeros/infinities, NaN payload behavior, literal
reciprocals, normal/subnormal output transition neighbors, representative
normal encodings, and source immutability. No host float/division oracle is
used.

Final Mac mini hardware acceptance must validate the `3/8192` relative-error
envelope for non-flushed normal outputs; it must not require exact equality
with this helper's bits. Keep the ambiguous tiny-result boundary as a separate
unresolved hardware question until the threshold text is clarified.

Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B RCPPS pp. 4-538–4-539 and RCPSS pp. 4-540–4-541
specify no SIMD FP exceptions, independence from MXCSR RC, signed-zero
interpretation for denormal sources, signed-zero flush for tiny results,
SNaN quieting/QNaN return, and relative error no greater than
`1.5 * 2^-12`. The published input-threshold inequalities overlap
contradictorily; see [ISSUE-025](../KNOWN_ISSUES.md#issue-025--intel-rcpssrcpps-threshold-inequalities-overlap).
Exact hardware behavior around the tiny-result boundary remains unresolved.
Full S2-36 and physical/Mac mini acceptance remain open.

#### S2-36ac — deterministic raw binary32 SSE reciprocal-square-root reference

Add `Binary32::reciprocal_sqrt_sse_raw()` as a pure deterministic value
reference. Signed zero and either-sign subnormal map to same-sign infinity
before checking input sign; negative normal values and negative infinity map
to negative indefinite QNaN; positive infinity maps to positive zero, inferred
from `1/sqrt(x)`. QNaN is returned unchanged and SNaN is quieted by setting its
quiet bit while preserving sign and payload as a local policy. Positive normal
inputs compose `sqrt_raw_result(NearestTiesEven)` and then
`reciprocal_sse_raw()` on the resulting value. Both intermediate and final
values remain normal. The method has no rounding argument or diagnostics and
does not mutate source, CPU state, or MXCSR, deliver SIMD exceptions, or
consult MXCSR.RC.

For positive normal inputs, each nearest-ties-even stage has relative error at
most `u=2^-24`; the composition is bounded by `2u/(1-u)`, less than Intel's
`1.5 * 2^-12` limit. This establishes only the error envelope, not exact or
hardware-matching result bits. An independent integer-only test uses the
24-bit significands `Mx` and `My` and unbiased exponents `ex` and `ey` to
check `(8192-3)^2 <= (Mx*My^2*2^(ex+2*ey-69))*8192^2 <= (8192+3)^2` by
u128 cross-multiplication. It does not use host floating point or production
helpers as an expected-value oracle.

Literal coverage includes `1→1`, `4→0.5`, `16→0.25`, `0.25→2`, min-normal
`2^-126→2^63`, signed zeros, every subnormal leading-bit position and sign,
infinities, varied QNaN/SNaN payloads, negative normals, source preservation,
and all positive normal exponent parities with representative significands.
Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B `RSQRTPS` pp. 4-594–4-595 and `RSQRTSS` pp.
4-596–4-597 specify the special cases, no SIMD FP exceptions, independence
from MXCSR.RC, and the `1.5 * 2^-12` relative-error bound. Positive-infinity
mapping and NaN payload/sign behavior are local inferences/policies where the
operation text does not fully define the result. [Official Intel Vol. 2B
PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241). Instruction dispatch,
packed lanes, MXCSR state, native/JIT, CPUID and physical-hardware acceptance
remain outside this slice.

#### S2-36y — bounded raw binary32/binary64 to signed i64 conversion

Add `Binary32::to_i64(mode)` and `Binary64::to_i64(mode)` as local value-only
conversions returning `BinaryIntegerResult<i64>`. Preserve the existing
`BinaryIntegerResult<T = i32>` default and the S2-36x i32 methods and results.
Round the exact finite source value first, then validate the rounded magnitude
against the signed i64 range. Both signed zeros produce exact zero. Non-finite
sources or rounded out-of-range values return the `i64::MIN` sentinel with
`invalid_operation=true` and `inexact=false`; exact `-2^63` remains a valid
result. Valid inexact conversions report a discarded fractional source part.
This helper does not mutate the source, CPU state, or MXCSR, and does not
deliver architectural exceptions.

Use one private integer-magnitude rounding helper for i32 and i64. Preserve the
common zero and exponent-below-zero cases, reject exponents above 63, and use
`rational_rounding::round_quotient_to_precision` for exponents 0 through 63 so
the 64-bit halfway case never constructs an overflowing shift. Keep typed
range checks and minimum-value formation in each wrapper; do not add a public
destination-width framework or x87/executor dependency.

Literal tests cover both source widths and all four modes, exact and fractional
values, exponents 31/32, 52/53, 62/63/64, huge finite values, and non-finite
classes. Boundary cases use the actual neighboring encodings around ±2^63:
binary32's largest positive value below 2^63 is 2^63−2^39, while binary64's is
2^63−1024. Do not posit fractional binary64 values between those neighboring
encodings. Verify valid exact `-2^63`, the invalid positive `2^63`, invalid
adjacent out-of-range encodings, invalid-result suppression of inexactness,
and source immutability. Preserve and rerun the unchanged S2-36x i32 suite.

Provenance: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSD2SI` p. 3-232,
`CVTSS2SI` p. 3-242, `CVTTSD2SI` p. 3-253, and `CVTTSS2SI` p. 3-255 specify
REX.W signed quadword conversion, rounding/truncation, and masked indefinite
behavior. This local helper does not implement MXCSR or architectural delivery.
Full S2-36/Stage 2 acceptance and hardware/Mac mini validation remain open.

### S2-37. SSE/SSE2 FP arithmetic и conversions

1. Добавлять scalar/packed arithmetic и comparisons, затем conversions в порядке таблицы профиля.
2. Применять MXCSR rounding и правила сохранения destination lanes; не распространять scalar effect на весь XMM.
3. Для approximate instructions использовать нормативные error bounds, для exact-result instructions — точное сравнение.

**Готово:** NaNs, infinities, signed zeros, subnormals, boundary conversions и обычные cases сопоставлены с Mac mini в поддерживаемых формах.

#### S2-37l — local Long64 register-only legacy MAXPD with masked status

Add schema-v2 profile `s2-long-maxpd-reg-masked-v1` for exactly one
`66 [optional one adjacent REX.R/B] 0F 5F /r` instruction, ModR/M.mod=3 and
XMM0–15. The operand-size prefix selects MAXPD; bare `0F 5F /r` remains MAXPS,
F3 remains MAXSS and F2 remains MAXSD. Keep all forms distinct in decoder
semantics and strict profile validation. Require SSE state, all six MXCSR
exception masks, DAZ/FTZ clear and reserved bits 16–31 clear; permit any RC and
old sticky bits.

Snapshot both complete XMM operands and use `Binary64::max_sse_raw_result` for
the two little-endian lanes. Either QNaN or SNaN selects raw operand 2 and
contributes IE. Same-lane invalid suppresses only that lane's new DE; aggregate
effective IE/DE across both lanes, preserving prior sticky status. Commit the
complete destination XMM and effective IE/DE only after preflight. Aliasing is
supported and no data-memory callback occurs. Missing SSE or unsupported MXCSR
refuses atomically. JIT/native/CPUID, memory forms and unmasked delivery remain
closed. Add all 256 register-pair, lane-order/alias, literal edge-case,
every-RC, sticky-status, refusal, strict-decoder/profile, literal-fixture,
native-denial and JIT-denial checks. Physical validation stays in the combined
final Mac mini substage. Results and remaining S2-37 coverage dependencies are
recorded in [the S2-37l report](../reports/S2_37L_MAXPD.md).

#### S2-37m — exact Long64 CVTDQ2PD XMM0,XMM1

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtdq2pd-reg-exact-v1`
accepts only `F3 0F E6 C1` (`CVTDQ2PD XMM0,XMM1`), one executable mapping,
budget one, and stop RIP `entry+4`. It refuses memory forms, REX/register
extensions, duplicate/reordered prefixes, other ModR/M operands, VEX and EVEX
forms. These profile refusals do not claim architectural #UD for each encoding.
Immutable SSE2, CR0.EM/TS, and CR4.OSFXSR inputs are echoed. Complete fetch
precedes #UD for missing SSE2, EM, or OSFXSR and then #NM for TS; the same
priority applies at CPL0–3. The fault retires zero instructions, preserves the
complete CPU snapshot, and causes no data-memory callback.

The two low signed i32 lanes of XMM1 (bits 31:0 and 63:32) are sign-extended
and converted exactly to binary64 in XMM0; XMM1 high64 is ignored. The full
XMM0 is replaced. MXCSR and all unrelated architectural state are preserved.
MXCSR accepts only the supported mask `0x0000ffbf`; all rounding, exception
mask, sticky status, and FTZ combinations produce the same result. There are
no SIMD floating-point exceptions, #XM gate, or x87/MMX transition.

Six handwritten fixtures cover zero, ±1, i32 endpoints, asymmetric lanes,
integer bit patterns resembling NaNs, and values around 2^24. Schema-v2 derives
expected result bits independently from integer bits and validates full state,
control echoes, exception/retirement metadata, exact bytes, budget and stop.
Focused ISA tests cover every SSE2/EM/TS/OSFXSR combination at CPL0–3, supported
MXCSR dimensions, malformed encodings, fetch truncation, STOP/budget, and no
data-memory access. JIT and native admission stay closed. Generic CPUID
admission, memory forms, complete S2-37, physical validation and parent
acceptance remain open. Physical checks are reserved for the combined final
Mac mini substage. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTDQ2PD pp. 3-208–3-210;
§2.5 Table 2-15 p. 2-24 and §2.5.5 Table 2-22 p. 2-30
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). See the
[CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37m--exact-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm0xmm1),
[stage report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37m--exact-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm0xmm1),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37m-local-cvtdq2pd).

#### S2-37p — canonical Long64 CVTDQ2PD XMM register pairs

Implemented the sibling interpreter-only schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-cvtdq2pd-registers-v1` accepts all 256 destination/source pairs
XMM0–15, including aliases, with canonical encodings `F3 0F E6 /r` for two
low registers and `F3 41/44/45 0F E6 /r` for source/destination/both high
registers. The independent schema parser derives both register indices and
instruction length from bytes; it requires one executable mapping, budget one,
and stop RIP `entry+length`, with checked address arithmetic. The preceding
S2-37m exact XMM0,XMM1 profile remains strict and unchanged.

Execution snapshots the source before writing the full destination, converts
the low two signed i32 lanes exactly to binary64, ignores source high64, and
preserves all other state. MXCSR support, four explicit SSE2/CR0/CR4 gates,
fault priority, and CPL0–3 behavior match S2-37m. JIT/native remain denied.
Tests cover all register pairs and aliases, extension classes, gates and
malformed/noncanonical forms. This is canonical register-pair coverage only;
m64 memory, other modes/encodings, physical acceptance, and S2-00/S2-38 parent
requirements remain open. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTDQ2PD
pp. 3-208–3-210; §2.2.1.2 pp. 2-8–2-9 and Table 2-4/Fig. 2-5
([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)). See the
[CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37p--canonical-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm-register-pairs),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37p--canonical-long64-cvtdq2pd-xmm-register-pairs),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37p-local-cvtdq2pd-register-pairs).

#### S2-37n — exact Long64 CVTSI2SD XMM0,EAX

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtsi2sd-r32-exact-v1` admits
only `F2 0F 2A C0` (`CVTSI2SD XMM0,EAX`), one executable mapping, budget one,
and stop RIP `entry+4`. It rejects REX/r64, other register indices, memory,
extra/reordered/repeated prefixes, other encodings, VEX and EVEX as profile
refusals; these do not assert architectural #UD for every excluded form. It
reads only RAX[31:0] as signed i32, sign-extends it, and performs exact
binary64 conversion. It replaces only XMM0[63:0], preserving XMM0[127:64],
full RAX, all unrelated state, RFLAGS/definedness and MXCSR. Supported MXCSR
bits are `0x0000ffbf`; accepted RC, masks, sticky flags and FTZ variations do
not affect the result. DAZ is architecturally irrelevant to this integer
source, but DAZ=1 is outside the local mask and is rejected. This r32 input is
always exactly representable, so this form raises no newly generated SIMD
Precision, Invalid or Denormal exception; PE masking and OSXMMEXCPT
do not create #XM/#UD. OSXMMEXCPT is echoed and both values are covered.
Complete fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD, then TS #NM at CPL0–3. Faults do
not retire, mutate state, or cause data-memory callbacks.

Eight literal fixtures cover 0, ±1, i32 endpoints, both sides of 2^24, equal
EAX with different RAX high halves, and full state preservation. The schema
oracle independently derives binary64 bits from the signed integer. Tests cover
all supported MXCSR combinations, prerequisite combinations at CPL0–3,
malformed/truncated forms, STOP/zero budget and fail-closed JIT/native. Only
this r32 register form is supported. Source: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A
`CVTSI2SD` pp. 3-236–3-237, Type 3 §2.5 Table 2-15, legacy gates §2.5.3
Table 2-20 p. 2-28 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).
See the [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37n--exact-long64-cvtsi2sd-xmm0eax),
[stage report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37n--exact-long64-cvtsi2sd-xmm0eax),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37n-local-cvtsi2sd-r32).

#### S2-37o — exact Long64 CVTSI2SD XMM0,RAX

Implement the interpreter-only schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-cvtsi2sd-r64-exact-v1` for only `F2 48 0F 2A C0`, one executable
mapping, budget one, and stop RIP `entry+5`. Keep S2-37n r32 separate. Other
REX values, r32, other GPR/XMM indices, memory, other/reordered/repeated
prefixes, other opcodes, VEX and EVEX are profile refusals, not generalized
architectural #UD claims.

Read the complete signed i64 from RAX and convert with `Binary64::from_i64`
under MXCSR.RC. Replace only XMM0 low64 on success; preserve its high64, RAX,
MXCSR except a newly sticky PE, and unrelated state. Accept only the existing
MXCSR mask `0x0000ffbf`; DAZ=1 and reserved bits reject. Only Precision may be
newly raised. For inexact results, set PE before delivery: PM=0 suppresses the
destination and retirement, then raises #XM if CR4.OSXMMEXCPT=1 or SIMD #UD
otherwise. PM=1 commits the rounded result and sticky PE. Exact results do not
fault from old PE. Preserve SSE2, CR0.EM/TS and CR4.OSFXSR prerequisite gates;
full fetch precedes #UD then #NM and prerequisite faults leave state unchanged.

Use an independent schema-v2 oracle based on signed magnitude, u128 remainder
bits and explicit nearest-even/directed rounding. Literal coverage includes
0, ±1, i64 endpoints, ±(2^53−1), ±2^53, ±(2^53+1), ±(2^53+3), midpoint
neighbors and carry across a power boundary. Verify all 4 RC × 2 PM × 2
OSXMMEXCPT × 2 old-PE combinations on representative exact and inexact values,
plus prerequisite CPL0–3, malformed/truncated encodings, STOP/budget, complete
state preservation, no data callbacks, schema/result/control tampering and
JIT/native denial. i64::MAX rounding to 2^63 is valid, not overflow.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSI2SD` pp. 3-236–3-237, Type 3 §2.5
Table 2-15 and §2.5.3 Table 2-20 p. 2-28; Vol. 1 §11.5.2.6 p. 11-16 and
§§11.5.3.1–3 pp. 11-16–11-18 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).
The full operand/register space, memory forms, full S2-37 and parent S2-34/S2-38
acceptance remain open; physical execution belongs to the combined final
hardware substage.

See the [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37o--exact-long64-cvtsi2sd-xmm0rax),
[stage report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37o--exact-long64-cvtsi2sd-xmm0rax),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37o-local-cvtsi2sd-r64).

#### S2-37q — canonical Long64 CVTSI2SD register operands

The interpreter-only schema-v2 sibling profile `s2-long-cvtsi2sd-registers-v1`
accepts 2 widths × 16 XMM destinations × 16 GPR sources, ModR/M.mod=3 only.
Its independent schema parser derives width, indices, and instruction length
from the complete byte stream. Canonical r32 uses `F2 0F 2A /r` for low
registers and `F2 41/44/45 0F 2A /r` for extended operands; r64 uses
`F2 48/49/4C/4D 0F 2A /r`. Redundant REX, X, incorrect W, noncanonical
prefixes, memory, trailing bytes, VEX, and EVEX are profile refusals, not
generalized #UD claims. S2-37n/o fixed profiles retain their restrictions.

r32 reads only the selected GPR low32 as signed i32, converts exactly, and
preserves the full GPR. r64 reads the selected signed i64 and reuses S2-37o
MXCSR rounding, sticky PE and unmasked delivery rules. Both widths update only
the selected XMM low64 and preserve its high64, all other XMMs and machine
state. RSP is an ordinary GPR source; the instruction performs no stack or
data-memory access. Existing SSE2, CR0.EM/TS, CR4.OSFXSR/OSXMMEXCPT gates and
MXCSR mask `0x0000ffbf` remain in force. Fixtures require one executable
mapping, budget 1, checked stop `entry+length`, and exact result/control echoes.
The schema oracle derives expected integer-to-binary64 results independently.

The schema-driven runner covers all 512 forms with distinct register sentinels,
including result and preservation checks. Memory forms m32/m64, other modes or
prefixes, generic CPUID admission, and physical acceptance remain open. All
hardware checks stay in the combined final substage. Sources: Intel SDM Rev.093
Vol.2A CVTSI2SD pp.3-236–3-237, Type 3 Table 2-20 p.2-28, Vol.1 §§11.5.2.6,
11.5.3, REX §2.2.1.2/Table 2-4 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).

#### S2-38a — consumed masked MINSS/MAXSS/MINPS/MAXPS/MINSD/MAXSD/MINPD/MAXPD status subset

Only masked IE/DE sticky-status updates used by S2-37e/f/g/h/i/j/k/l are implemented.
MINSS/MAXSS/MINSD/MAXSD apply invalid-over-denormal priority within their scalar
operation. MINPS/MAXPS first apply that priority per lane, then OR effective
IE/DE across their four lanes. MINPD/MAXPD apply the same per-lane priority and
aggregation across two lanes before the single atomic destination and MXCSR commit;
pre-existing sticky status is preserved. Full S2-38 remains open: unmasked exception delivery, #XM
behavior, CR0/CR4 and OSXMMEXCPT gating, memory/alignment/FP fault priority,
precise fault ordering, and the remaining MXCSR/SSE exception surface are not
implemented or claimed. Final physical checks stay in the combined Mac mini
substage.

#### S2-37r — canonical Long64 CVTSI2SS register operand space

The interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtsi2ss-registers-v1` admits
512 canonical ModR/M.mod=3 forms: r32/r64 × XMM0–15 × GPR0–15. r32 uses `F3`
for low registers and `F3 41/44/45` when the source and/or destination is
extended; r64 uses `F3 48/49/4C/4D`, with W selecting signed i64. Redundant
`40`, X, noncanonical W, repeated/reordered/other prefixes, memory, extra
bytes, VEX and EVEX are profile refusals, not generalized architectural #UD
claims. S2-37n/o/p/q remain separate profiles with their existing scope.

The executor reads signed low32 or full signed i64, ignores high32 for r32,
and preserves every source GPR. It rounds directly to binary32 using MXCSR.RC,
updates only destination XMM low32, and preserves its upper96 and all other
state. Either width can newly raise Precision. PE is sticky; PM=1 commits, and
PM=0 commits PE before #XM (OSXMMEXCPT=1) or SIMD-generated #UD otherwise,
without destination/RIP update or retirement. Old PE alone does not fault.
Only MXCSR bits in `0x0000ffbf` are accepted; DAZ/reserved bits reject and FTZ
does not affect conversion. SSE availability, CR0.EM/TS and CR4.OSFXSR gates
follow full fetch and precede conversion at CPL0–3. No data-memory access is
performed; RSP is an ordinary source. Generic capability and JIT/native/C/
fragment execution remain denied.

The schema oracle uses signed magnitude/u128, a 24-bit significand, explicit
remainder/halfway tests and directed rounding; it does not call production
conversion or host floating point. Literal anchors cover ±(2^24−1), ±2^24,
±(2^24+1), ±(2^24+3), i32/i64 endpoints, halfway neighbors, exponent carry,
and an integer where direct conversion differs from binary64 double rounding.
Runner coverage iterates all 512 forms with distinct GPR/XMM sentinels,
upper96/source preservation, both-width precision matrices, RSP, prerequisite
gates, malformed forms, result/control tampering and JIT/native denial. ISA
coverage additionally executes signed boundary, halfway/tie, i64 carry and
direct-vs-double-rounding literals across RC; an exact old-PE/PM=0 case must
complete. It also checks STOP, zero budget and truncated fetch before
prerequisites. Memory forms and other modes/prefixes remain open.

Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `CVTSI2SS` pp. 3-238–3-239, Type 3
Table 2-15/Table 2-20 p. 2-28; Vol. 1 §§11.5.2.6 and 11.5.3; REX §2.2.1.2
and Table 2-4 ([official PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199)).
See the [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37r--canonical-long64-cvtsi2ss-register-operand-space),
[report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37r--canonical-long64-cvtsi2ss-register-operand-space),
and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37r-canonical-cvtsi2ss-register-space).

#### S2-37s — canonical Long64 CVTDQ2PS XMM register pairs

Implement a separate strict schema-v2 interpreter profile for all 256
destination/source pairs XMM0–15, including aliases. Canonical legacy bytes are
`0F 5B /r` for low registers and exactly `41`, `44`, or `45` REX for an
extended source and/or destination. Require ModR/M.mod=3, one executable code
mapping, budget one and checked stop RIP `entry+length`. Reject other prefixes,
memory forms, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX as profile refusals; do not broaden
architectural #UD claims or alter the prior profiles.

Snapshot all four signed i32 source lanes before writing and convert directly
to binary32 with MXCSR.RC. Aggregate lane inexactness into PE. Preserve all
other MXCSR bits. Unmasked new PE commits sticky PE first and suppresses the
whole destination, RIP advance and retirement before #XM/#UD selection by
OSXMMEXCPT; masked or exact completion commits all lanes. Old PE alone does
not fault. Gates follow full fetch: missing SSE2, CR0.EM and CR4.OSFXSR produce
#UD, then CR0.TS produces #NM, independent of CPL; no data callbacks occur.

Tests must validate every register pair, aliases, all 16 lane-inexact masks ×
RC × PM × OSXMMEXCPT × prior PE, rounding anchors, gate/fetch ordering and
strict encoding refusals. Keep JIT/native/C/fragment and generic CPUID admission
closed. Memory m128, its alignment/fault behavior, other modes and physical
acceptance remain open; this bounded register slice does not close parent S2-37
or Stage 2.

#### S2-37 required legacy SSE/SSE2 arithmetic, comparison and conversion inventory

**Profile decision (2026-10-29):** the selected synthetic CPU target is Generic
`amd64` / x86-64-v1 and advertises SSE and SSE2. Therefore every legacy SSE/SSE2
form below is target-required in Long64, whether or not the examined Linux boot
path reaches it. This is a normative target inventory, not an implementation
claim or a complete inventory of every SSE/SSE2 instruction family. S2-37bi
scanned the authenticated built-in Ubuntu kernel ELF and found no decoded
inventory mnemonics in its five kernel code sections; this does not change
target requirements. Modules, initramfs and userspace are not mapped, and
runtime observation remains `not_run`. The versioned results are in the
[S2-37 Linux static-map manifest](../reports/data/stage2/s2-37-linux-vmlinux-map-v1.json)
and [Linux profile report](../reports/STAGE_2_LINUX_PROFILE.md#s2-37bi--static-mapping-of-s2-37-forms-in-the-ubuntu-kernel-elf).
Neither static absence from this kernel nor target-contract selection proves
physical acceptance. Source basis is Intel SDM Rev. 093, September 2026, Vol. 2A
253666-093US, instructions ADDPD through DIVSS (pp. 3-16–3-275), and Vol. 2B
253667-093US, MAXPD through UCOMISS (pp. 4-5–4-735). The Vol. 2A source is
[official Intel PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199); the
Vol. 2B source is [official Intel PDF](https://cdrdv2.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671241).

`/r` marks the ModR/M register-or-memory operand; the register class and memory
width are defined by each row. `NP` means no mandatory prefix. Unless noted,
destinations are XMM; scalar arithmetic/conversion forms preserve the other
destination lanes as specified by the instruction. The opcode and feature
columns below are legacy encodings only; VEX/EVEX forms are outside this
inventory.
