This is deliberately a masked-range profile. Admission requires MXCSR.OM=1 and
MXCSR.UM=1 in both schema and public runtime API because the existing raw
rounding result cannot distinguish exact-significand overflow from its bounded
masked-overflow response when OM=0. DAZ and reserved MXCSR bits are rejected;
all RC values, FTZ, IM/DM/PM and old sticky bits are accepted. Do not claim
complete unmasked overflow/underflow behavior.

Each lane computes old destination minus source from snapshots of both source
and destination XMM. Classify NaNs before sign-flipping the subtrahend: SNaN
raises IE and is quieted by the local helper policy, QNaN alone does not raise
IE, and NaN suppresses DE for that lane. Opposite-effective-sign infinities
raise IE and return the masked indefinite. Otherwise any subnormal operand
raises precompute DE. Aggregate IE/DE over both lanes before arithmetic; a new
unmasked pre-event commits generated IE/DE and faults without adding any new
OE/UE/PE or writing either lane. With pre-events masked, compute both lanes
using MXCSR.RC. Masked overflow reports OE|PE; underflow with an inexact tiny
result reports UE|PE, and FTZ can flush a tiny result to signed zero with
UE|PE. Aggregate PE and deliver an unmasked PE atomically. Old sticky flags
alone never fault. Successful execution replaces the full XMM destination.

Use an independent raw-u64 integer subtraction/rounding oracle without host FP
or production helpers. Tests cover the literal fixture, all 256 pairs and
aliases, NaN/infinity/subnormal ordering, cross-lane IE/DE suppression of post
flags, RC and signed-zero behavior, exact-overflow classification versus the
accepted OM=1 OE|PE response, FTZ tiny results, masks/stickies, atomic faults,
fetch/gates/CPL/STOP/budget/no-callback behavior, malformed encodings, result
tampering and backend denial. Focused checks and workspace checks passed;
independent review is clean. Physical acceptance, memory forms and other modes remain open, and parent
S2-37/S2-38 are not closed. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B SUBPD
pp. 4-687–4-689 and Vol. 2A p. 2-27 ([official SDM](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671199));
Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.3 and DAZ/FTZ ([Vol. 1](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671436));
Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8 ([Vol. 3A](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/671190));
Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13 ([PDF](https://cdrdv.intel.com/v1/dl/getContent/786447?fileName=floating-point-reference-sheet-for-intel-architecture.pdf)).

#### S2-37ar — bounded masked-range Long64 MULPD XMM register pairs

Implement strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile
`s2-long-mulpd-registers-v1` for canonical Long64 `66 0F 59 /r`, ModR/M.mod=3,
covering all 256 XMM destination/source pairs. Low forms are four bytes;
extended indices require exactly one REX `41`, `44`, or `45` immediately after
`66`, for length five. Reject memory, F2/F3, reordered/repeated/redundant
prefixes, REX.W/X/40, trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX. Fetch the complete encoding
before SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD and then TS #NM at CPL0–3; issue no data callbacks.
Keep JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic paths closed.

This is a bounded masked-range profile. Require MXCSR.OM=1 and MXCSR.UM=1 in
schema and runtime because the available rounding diagnostics do not represent
full unmasked overflow/underflow delivery. Reject DAZ and reserved MXCSR bits;
accept all RC settings, FTZ, IM/DM/PM and old sticky flags.

Each lane multiplies old destination by source from two pre-execution XMM
snapshots. Result sign is XOR. NaN propagation selects the first original
operand, quiets a selected SNaN, and raises IE for any SNaN; QNaN alone does not
raise IE, and NaNs suppress lane DE. Zero×infinity raises IE and produces the
masked Intel indefinite. Otherwise any subnormal operand raises precompute DE,
including zero×subnormal and infinity×subnormal. Aggregate IE/DE for both lanes
before arithmetic; an unmasked pre-event commits only generated IE/DE and
preserves XMM, RIP and retirement. With pre-events masked, use the production
raw binary64 multiply helper and MXCSR.RC. Overflow records OE|PE under this
OM=1 profile. Determine tininess from the exponent of the precision-rounded
result with unbounded exponent (WPR.exp), not from the exact product exponent.
For `0x0010000000000001 × 0x3feffffffffffffe`, RN/RU produce minimum-normal
with PE only regardless of FTZ; RD/RZ produce maximum-subnormal with UE|PE, or
positive zero with UE|PE under FTZ. The separate midpoint product
`minimum-normal × (1−2^-53)` remains tiny after precision rounding and retains
UE|PE in every RC mode. FTZ flushes a nonzero result whose WPR exponent is tiny.
Aggregate and commit status
before unmasked PE delivery; preserve the complete destination on faults.
The adjacent SUBPD profile already classifies tininess from the production
precision-rounded unbounded-exponent diagnostic; this erratum changes MULPD's
incorrect exact-product override only.

The schema oracle must independently multiply raw finite significands with
integer arithmetic, round to precision with unbounded exponent to classify
tininess, then apply bounded subnormal rounding; do not use host FP or
production helpers.
Cover all pairs and aliases, NaN ordering/quieting, inf/zero/subnormal cases,
XOR signs, exact/inexact tiny results and FTZ, all RC modes, production halfway
rounding, signed overflow direction, pre/post event priority, sticky flags,
masks, atomicity, fetch/gates/CPL/STOP/budget/no-callback behavior, malformed
prefixes, result tampering and backend denial. A local fixture and focused tests
are not physical acceptance. Memory forms, other modes, full unmasked OE/UE,
and parent S2-37/S2-38 remain open. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2B MULPD
pp. 4-142–4-143; Vol. 2A Type 2, Table 2-19; Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.3 and
DAZ/FTZ; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8; Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13.

#### S2-37as — bounded masked-range Long64 MULPS XMM register pairs

Require MXCSR.OM=1 and MXCSR.UM=1 in schema and runtime because complete
unmasked overflow/underflow delivery is outside the profile. Reject DAZ and
reserved MXCSR bits; accept all RC settings, FTZ, IM/DM/PM and old sticky flags.
Snapshot destination and source XMM before computing all four binary32 lanes.
NaN propagation selects the first operand, quiets a selected SNaN, and raises
IE for either SNaN; QNaN alone does not raise IE and suppresses same-lane DE.
Zero×infinity raises IE and produces `0xffc00000`; otherwise any subnormal

trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX. Fetch the complete encoding before SSE/EM/OSFXSR
#UD then TS #NM, at CPL0–3; make no data callbacks. Keep JIT/native/C ABI/
fragment/generic paths closed.

Require MXCSR.OM=1 and MXCSR.UM=1 in schema and runtime. Reject DAZ and reserved
MXCSR bits; accept every RC mode, FTZ, IM/DM/ZM/PM and old sticky flags. Snapshot
both XMM operands and compute all four old-destination/source Binary32 lanes.
NaNs select the first original operand; quiet a selected SNaN and raise IE for
any SNaN; NaNs suppress same-lane ZE/DE. `0/0` and `∞/∞` raise IE and return
the masked indefinite `ffc00000`. Finite nonzero or subnormal numerator over
zero raises ZE only; `∞/0` returns signed infinity without ZE. In all remaining
cases, any subnormal operand raises precompute DE, including `0/subnormal`,
`∞/subnormal`, and `subnormal/∞`. Aggregate IE/ZE/DE across all four lanes
before arithmetic; any unmasked pre-event commits all generated pre-flags and
preserves the whole destination, RIP and retirement. Otherwise use the
production `Binary32::divide_raw_result` under MXCSR.RC. Masked overflow sets
OE|PE. Tininess and FTZ use WPR's unbounded exponent after p=24 precision
rounding: tiny inexact results set UE|PE; FTZ flushes tiny nonzero results to
signed zero with UE|PE. Aggregate post flags across lanes; unmasked PM commits
flags then faults atomically. Old sticky flags alone do not fault.

Use an independent raw-u32 exact-rational oracle, with no host FP or production
helpers. Bound large shifts and round only once. The literal fixture covers
`1/3` (`3f800000/40400000`): RN/RU give `3eaaaaab`, RD/RZ give `3eaaaaaa`,
with PE. `minnormal/2^24` rounds to zero for RN/RD/RZ and minimum-subnormal for
RU, with UE|PE and no DE. The exact midpoint vector `00ffffff/40000000` returns minnormal for RN/RU and
maxsub for RD/RZ, with UE|PE. `minnormal/nextafter(1,+)` returns maxsub for RN/RD/RZ and
minnormal for RU, with UE|PE. Exact `minnormal/2` returns `00400000` without
flags. `minsub/maxfinite` rounds up to one only under RU and raises DE|UE|PE.
Cover all RC and FTZ boundaries, fourth-lane overflow/underflow, all pairs and
aliases, NaN payloads/SNaNs, signed zeros/infinities, ZE/DE priorities, sticky
flags, lane permutations, pre/post atomicity, gates/fetch/CPL/no-callback,
malformed/tampered inputs and JIT/native denial. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093
Vol. 2A DIVPS pp. 3-270–3-272 and the legacy SSE rows in Table 2-19; the
explicit Type 2/Table 2-19 cross-reference on p. 3-272 applies to VEX forms and
is not applied to legacy DIVPS. Generic exception-gate documentation and Vol. 1
§§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.2–11.5.3, DAZ/FTZ; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8; Intel
Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13. This local profile does not claim memory
forms, alignment, physical acceptance, other modes, full unmasked OE/UE
behavior or closure of parent S2-37/S2-38. See the [CPU

#### S2-37az — canonical Long64 ADDPD XMM register pairs

Implement strict schema-v2 interpreter-only profile
`s2-long-addpd-registers-v1` for canonical Long64 legacy `66 0F 58 /r`,
ModR/M.mod=3, covering all 256 XMM pairs. Low forms are four bytes; extended
indices require exactly one REX `41`, `44` or `45` after 66, for five bytes.
Reject memory, F2/F3, reordered/repeated/redundant prefixes, REX.W/X/40,
trailing bytes, VEX and EVEX. Fetch the complete instruction before SSE2/EM/
OSFXSR #UD then TS #NM at CPL0–3; issue no data callbacks. Keep JIT/native/C
ABI/fragment/generic paths closed.

Require MXCSR.OM=1 and UM=1 in schema and runtime. Reject DAZ/reserved MXCSR
bits; accept RC, FTZ, IM/DM/ZM/PM and old sticky flags. Snapshot both XMM
operands and compute two old-destination plus source binary64 lanes. NaNs
select the first original operand, quiet a selected SNaN, and raise IE for any
SNaN; NaNs suppress same-lane DE. Opposite-sign infinities raise IE and return
the masked indefinite `fff8000000000000`; other infinity results retain their
sign. Any subnormal finite operand raises DE, including infinity plus
subnormal. Aggregate IE/DE before arithmetic; an unmasked pre-event commits
all generated pre-flags and suppresses every post flag and the full destination
write. Otherwise use `Binary64::add_raw_result` with MXCSR.RC. Exact
cancellation is -0 only under round-down; same-sign zeros retain their sign.
Masked overflow records OE|PE; directed overflow to maxfinite may record PE
only when rounding the overflow-boundary midpoint does not itself exceed the
exponent range. A larger exact result such as maxfinite+maxfinite records
OE|PE even when directed rounding returns maxfinite. Determine tininess after
precision rounding. A finite same-format binary64 sum is an integer multiple
of minsub, so an unflushed subnormal result is exact and raises no UE/PE. FTZ
flushes only tiny nonzero results to signed zero with UE|PE. Aggregate post
flags; unmasked PM commits status but preserves XMM/RIP/retirement. Old sticky
flags alone never fault.

Use an independent raw-u64 integer oracle. Its finite path adds exact signed
integer magnitudes and rounds once; special-value classification remains
independent from production helpers. Cover all pairs and aliases; NaN payloads
and SNaNs; opposite infinities; infinity plus subnormal; positive and negative
halfway rounding; exact and FTZ tiny sums; signed-zero rules; large exponent
gaps; masked and directed overflow; lane permutations; sticky flags; cross-lane
IE/DE suppression of other-lane OE/PE/FTZ-UE; fetch/gate/CPL/STOP/budget/no-
callback behavior; malformed/tampered fixtures; and backend denial. The
handwritten literal fixture covers `1 + 2^-53` and `1 + (-0)`. The oracle and
runner matrices additionally cover exact tiny
`0010000000000001 + 8010000000000000` (minsub without flags, FTZ zero with
UE|PE), overflow midpoint `7fefffffffffffff + 7c90000000000000` (RN/RU
infinity with OE|PE; RD/RZ maxfinite with PE only), and maxfinite+maxfinite
(OE|PE in every rounding mode, including directed maxfinite responses).

#### S2-37be — canonical Long64 CVTSD2SS XMM register pairs

Implemented the interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtsd2ss-registers-v1` for all 256 Long64 XMM destination/source pairs. It accepts legacy `F2 [canonical optional REX 41/44/45] 0F 5A /r`, ModR/M.mod=3, with lengths 4/5. Memory, VEX/EVEX, malformed, redundant or reordered prefixes and trailing bytes are refused. Full fetch precedes SSE2/EM/OSFXSR #UD and TS #NM at CPL0–3; there are no data callbacks. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic admission remains closed.

The scalar conversion snapshots source.low64 before writing, converts binary64 to binary32 under MXCSR.RC using `Binary32::narrow_from_binary64`, writes destination.low32 and preserves destination[127:32]. Source.high64 and old destination do not affect arithmetic; source snapshots make aliases safe. MXCSR admission requires OM=UM=1, DAZ=0 and reserved bits clear. SNaN raises IE, a binary64 subnormal raises DE, overflow raises OE|PE, tiny inexact results raise UE|PE, and FTZ flushes tiny nonzero results to signed zero with UE|PE, including exact tiny results as specified by the Intel Floating-Point Reference Sheet v2.13 p.2. Unmasked IE/DE stops before conversion post-events; unmasked OE/UE/PE records status but preserves destination, RIP and retirement. OSXMMEXCPT selects #XM or SIMD-generated #UD for numeric faults.

The independent schema-v2 oracle uses raw integer classification and rounding, separate from the production helper and host floating point. Local tests cover all pairs and aliases, source/destination poison, all RC/tie and normal/subnormal boundaries, FTZ, overflow, QNaN/SNaN sign/payload, DE/IE/PE masks and sticky status, atomic faults, gates/fetch/CPL/no-callbacks, malformed encodings, result/schema validation and JIT/native denial. #### S2-37bg — canonical Long64 CVTPI2PS memory-only RAX

Реализован interpreter-only schema-v2 профиль `s2-long-cvtpi2ps-memory-rax-v1` для точной формы `0F 2A 00`; budget=1, stop RIP=entry+3. Он отклоняет MMX register source, другие ModR/M/addressing forms, любой prefix/REX, VEX/EVEX и trailing bytes. Полная выборка трёх байт предшествует SSE/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD и затем CR0.TS #NM.

При RFLAGS.AC=0 профиль требует SSE state, MXCSR в mask `0x0000ffbf` с PM=1 и x87 snapshot без pending exceptions (`FSW & 0x80ff == 0`). До чтения не допускаются состояния вне этих границ. После проверок выполняется один 8-byte read из canonical48 `[RAX..RAX+7]`; две little-endian signed i32 lane напрямую конвертируются в binary32 с MXCSR.RC. Записываются только XMM0.low64, high64 сохраняется. PE агрегируется по обеим lanes и устанавливается sticky. Успешная инструкция всегда устанавливает x87 TOP=0 и tag_word=0, сохраняя регистровые payloads, CW, указатели, opcode и остальные FSW bits. Все изменения CPU отложены до успешного read; ошибку локального read профиль возвращает без частичного commit. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic dispatch не допускаются.

Независимый schema oracle округляет signed i32 к binary32 целочисленными операциями. Focused проверки покрывают все четыре RC, положительные/отрицательные ties и границы 2^24, экстремумы i32, обе комбинации PE, prior sticky flags, все TOP и четыре кодировки x87 tag-классов, сохранение x87/MMX payloads и указателей, unaligned read с AC=0, pending-x87/PM=0/AC=1 отказ без data read, единственный read, rollback после read failure, gate priority, malformed bytes, backend denial и tampering. Физическая x86-приёмка остаётся открытой.

Источники: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A CVTPI2PS p. 3-224; Vol. 3B §25.25.3 Table 25-5 p. 25-23; Vol. 1 SSE, MXCSR rounding, precision exception и x87/MMX shared state. См. [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37bg--canonical-long64-cvtpi2ps-memory-only-rax), [отчёт](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37bg--cvtpi2ps-memory-interpreter-profile) и [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37bg-cvtpi2ps-memory-rax-profile).


#### S2-37bf — canonical Long64 CVTPI2PD memory-only RAX

Implemented interpreter-only schema-v2 profile `s2-long-cvtpi2pd-memory-rax-v1` for the exact four-byte form `66 0F 2A 00`; it executes one instruction with budget 1 and stop RIP=entry+4. All register-source, alternate ModR/M/addressing, REX, additional/reordered prefixes, VEX/EVEX, trailing bytes and non-Long64 forms are refused. Full instruction fetch has priority over SSE2-unavailable/CR0.EM/CR4.OSFXSR #UD, followed by CR0.TS #NM, and all gates precede the single data read.

It ignores old XMM0 and preserves all other CPU state, including MXCSR and x87 tags/TOP; this memory-source operation does not deliver a pending x87 exception and raises no SIMD FP exception. It writes no memory. AC-set is outside the profile. An injected local read failure rolls back locally; guest #PF delivery is not claimed. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic dispatch remain denied.

The independent schema oracle builds binary64 bits using integer operations. Decoder/interpreter tests and a literal schema-v2 runner fixture cover ±0/±1, i32 extrema, 2^24 boundaries, asymmetric lanes, NaN-shaped integers, arbitrary/pending x87 state, exact read size/count, canaries, unaligned data with AC clear, canonical overflow, local read failure, gate/fetch ordering, STOP/budget, malformed/tampered metadata/results and backend denial. `cargo test -p od-isa cvtpi2pd --offline`, `cargo test -p od-runner cvtpi2pd_memory_profile --offline`, formatting, workspace check, layout validation, diff check and Graphify update passed. #### S2-37br — bounded Long64 CVTPD2PI MM0,[RAX] aligned m128 memory profile

**Status: implemented and verified locally.** Add separate
schema-v2 interpreter-only profile `s2-long-cvtpd2pi-memory-rax-v1` for exact
`66 0F 2D 00`, budget=1 and stop RIP=entry+4. Fetch all four instruction
bytes before profile #UD for missing SSE2 (CPUID bit 26), CR0.EM or CR4.OSFXSR,
then #NM for CR0.TS; this ordering is bounded local policy. CPL0–3 are accepted.

Read exactly one 16-byte m128 from RAX after checking the entire canonical48
span and 16-byte alignment. Misalignment raises #GP(0) before memory callbacks
at any CPL regardless of RFLAGS.AC; it does not raise #AC. Aligned sources are
accepted with AC clear or set. Require MXCSR bits within `0xffbf`, IM=PM=1, and
`FSW & 0x80ff == 0`; pending x87 exceptions are rejected by strict local
admission, and #MF delivery is not modeled.

Round each binary64 lane to signed i32 according to MXCSR.RC, then test whether
the rounded integer is representable. This ordering matters near the endpoints:
`0x41dfffffffffffff` rounds out of range for nearest/up but remains
`i32::MAX` for down/toward-zero; `0xc1e0000000000001` rounds out of range only
for down, while nearest/up/toward-zero produce valid `i32::MIN`. Out-of-range,
NaN and infinity produce `0x80000000` and sticky IE. A valid inexact rounded
result sets sticky PE; flags aggregate across lanes, incoming status/control
bits are preserved, and DE is not raised. After one successful read, write the
pair to physical MM0 with exponent word `ffff`, set TOP=0/all tags valid, and
preserve other x87 state. Read failure leaves CPU state unchanged. Native/JIT/C
ABI and broader forms remain closed.

The independent testkit oracle classifies raw u64 bits using integer operations
only, with no host FP or production conversion helper. Literal fixture and
runner matrix cover all RC values, both post-rounding endpoint cases, mixed
IE+PE generation from clear flags, sticky histories, aligned CPL×AC, the 15
misalignment offsets at representative CPL/AC, TOP/tag canaries, malformed and
tampered inputs, and backend denial. Direct ISA tests cover all offset×CPL×AC
misalignment cases with no read/state change, aligned success, one exact 16-byte
read, pre-read gate/span refusals, full fetch and read-failure rollback. No
physical x86 acceptance is claimed.

#### S2-37ca — bounded Long64 CVTSD2SS XMM0,[RAX] m64 memory profile

Exact legacy bytes are `F2 0F 5A 00`; the schema-v2 profile
`s2-long-cvtsd2ss-memory-rax-v1` admits Long64, full four-byte fetch, budget
one, and stop RIP=entry+4. Local SSE2 (CPUID bit 26), EM/OSFXSR #UD, then TS
#NM gate ordering is bounded profile policy; CPL0–3 are admitted. RAX names one
checked canonical48 m64 span. Exactly one 8-byte read occurs after preflight;
unaligned reads are allowed at local AC=0. A failed read leaves CPU state
unchanged. Missing SSE state is a local Unsupported refusal after prerequisite
gates and before the data read.

The binary64 source rounds to binary32 according to MXCSR.RC. Tininess uses
WPR: round to 24-bit precision with unbounded exponent first, then test the
result before final exponent encoding. Consequently a WPR-normal rounded value
can encode as minimum normal and still avoid UE, while a WPR-tiny value can
encode as minimum normal and still raise UE|PE. FTZ flushes every WPR-tiny
nonzero result to signed zero and raises UE|PE, even when the precision result
was exact; FTZ does not flush WPR-normal results. Overflow and tiny/inexact
conditions use masked IE/DE/OE/UE/PE status only; invalid lanes do not add PE.
NaNs preserve sign, SNaNs are quieted with the payload narrowed as specified
by Table D-12, and QNaNs add no IE/PE. DAZ=0 means nonzero binary64
subnormals contribute DE and may also underflow during narrowing. Only XMM0.low32
is replaced; all other XMM0 bits, MXCSR controls and unrelated state are
preserved. x87 is neither gated nor modified.

Local admission requires MXCSR supported mask `0xffbf`, DAZ=0 and IM/DM/OM/UM/PM=1;
ZM may be clear. AC=1 is a local Unsupported refusal, not an architectural
alignment claim. No unmasked SIMD delivery is modeled. Independent testkit
oracle uses integer raw-bit operations, not host FP or production conversion
helpers. JIT/native/C ABI/fragment/generic execution remain closed. Verification passed: the focused ISA suite passed 5/5 and full od-isa 1,628/1,628;
the focused runner passed 1/1 (455 filtered), with 168 raw-input × RC × FTZ
cases; full od-testkit passed 446/446 with 0 doc-tests; full od-runner passed
112 unit + 456 fixture tests; full od-x86-runner passed 8 library + 4 binary
tests. The post-review exact-tiny ISA and runner tests passed 1/1 each; an
independent no-compile CLI smoke passed 176/176. Workspace all-target check,
formatting, diff check, layout validation and Graphify refresh passed.
Independent review completed without remaining findings. Physical x86 acceptance
is not claimed.

#### S2-37cf — exact legacy Long64 CVTSI2SS XMM0,qword ptr [RAX]

profile uses SSE CPUID bit 25, with local fetch→`#UD`→`#NM` ordering for exact
profile gates and CPL0–3.

and AC=0; all RC/FTZ settings, other supported masks, and old sticky state are
admitted. PM=0/DAZ=1/reserved MXCSR bits are malformed schema input. AC=1 is a

read or state mutation. Missing SSE state after prerequisite gates also fails
closed as `Unsupported`. The independent oracle parses fixture memory as raw
i64 and uses integer-only rounding. JIT/native/C ABI/generic execution remain

The literal fixture and independent integer-only raw-u32 oracle cover the
four-lane memory source, all RC settings and old sticky patterns. Expanded
runner vectors cover NaN payload/sign and SNaN-vs-QNaN priority, denormal
priority, opposite infinities, RC-sensitive ties, cancellation and signed zero,
the tiny boundary, overflow, mixed-lane IE/DE/OE/PE aggregation, RHS-only
negative QNaN payload/sign preservation, NaN suppression of same-lane DE, and
RC-dependent cancellation zero. UE cannot be newly raised by finite binary32
subtraction: every finite binary32 operand and exact result is an integer
multiple of `q = 2^-149`. If the exact result magnitude is below `2^-126`, its
integer coefficient has magnitude below `2^23`, so it is exactly representable
as a subnormal or zero. This proves exactness for tiny results both inside and
outside Sterbenz's factor-of-two range, including opposite-sign sums. The full
sticky matrix still verifies preservation of an incoming UE bit. Full suites passed:

marker and two existing absent oracle manifests linked from `STAGE_2_REPORT.md`;
the slice adds no paths. Independent Sol/high follow-up review is pending the
coverage commit. Physical x86 acceptance is not claimed. See
[standalone report](../reports/S2_37DR_SUBPS_MEMORY.md) and

#### S2-37di — masked-only Long64 ADDSS XMM0,m32 [RAX]

Implement the strict schema-v2 local interpreter profile `s2-long-addss-memory-rax-v1` for exactly `F3 0F 58 00`, length four, instruction budget one, and stop RIP entry+4. Require Long64, legacy SSE (`CPUID.01H:EDX[25]`), CR0.EM=0, CR4.OSFXSR=1, CR0.TS=0, and XMM/MXCSR state. Fetch all four instruction bytes before gates; missing SSE, EM=1, or OSFXSR=0 raises #UD before TS=1 raises #NM. Reject all other prefixes, REX, ModR/M/addressing forms, VEX/EVEX, truncation, trailing bytes and non-XMM0 forms.

Admit only supported MXCSR bits `0xffbf`, with reserved bits clear, all six exception masks set, DAZ=FTZ=0. Any RC mode and any prior IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE sticky history are allowed. Unmasked exceptions and #XM delivery are not modeled. AC=1 returns local Unsupported before address validation or data reads; AC=0 admits unaligned m32. Check checked-add overflow and canonical48 endpoints for `[RAX,RAX+3]` before exactly one read4. A read error preserves complete CPU/SSE/MXCSR/RIP state and retirement.

Compute `old XMM0.low32 + loaded m32` with the existing `Binary32::add_raw_result(MXCSR.RC)`. This is a true two-operand add: memory supplies RHS and XMM0.low32 supplies LHS. Preserve XMM0.high96, XMM1 and all unrelated state. Apply the existing ADDSS raw register semantics for generated IE/DE/OE/UE/PE and OR those bits into old MXCSR sticky state; do not apply MINSS/SQRTSS flag priority. Success advances RIP by four and retires exactly once. JIT/native/C ABI/generic/fragment execution remains closed.

The independent testkit `independent_addss` oracle receives the literal memory RHS and uses raw integer arithmetic, not host floating point or the production helper. The halfway fixture poisons XMM1, sets XMM0.high96 canaries and exercises `1 + 2^-24`. Direct execution coverage crosses all four RC settings with all 64 prior sticky histories across halfway/adjacent values, exponent gaps, tiny/subnormal sums, NaNs, infinities, signed zeros and overflow. Address/gate ordering, no-read AC refusal, canonical endpoint crossing, u64 endpoint overflow, one read4, read-failure rollback, malformed schema/provenance/result tampering, register ADDSS regression and JIT/native denial are checked.

No physical x86 acceptance is claimed. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A ADDSS pp. 3-24–3-25 and legacy SSE rows in Table 2-27; Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.2–11.5.3 and DAZ/FTZ; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8. The p. 3-25 Type 3/Table 2-20 note applies to VEX forms; legacy SSE capability and exception claims use the legacy rows. See the [CPU contract](../specs/CPU_CONTRACT.md#s2-37di--masked-only-long64-addss-xmm0m32-rax), [shared report](../reports/STAGE_2_REPORT.md#s2-37di--addss-xmm0m32-rax), [standalone implementation report](../reports/S2_37DI_ADDSS_MEMORY.md), and [fixture notes](../../tests/fixtures/x86/stage2/README.md#s2-37di--addss-xmm0m32-rax).


#### S2-37dj — masked-only legacy `Long64` `ADDSD` XMM0,m64 [RAX]

Implement strict schema-v2 local interpreter profile `s2-long-addsd-memory-rax-v1` for exactly `F2 0F 58 00`, four bytes, instruction budget one, and stop RIP entry+4. Require `Long64`, `SSE2` (`CPUID.01H:EDX[26]`), `CR0.EM=0`, `CR4.OSFXSR=1`, `CR0.TS=0`, and XMM/`MXCSR` state. Fetch all four bytes before local gates; absent `SSE2`, EM=1 or OSFXSR=0 raises `#UD` before TS=1 raises `#NM`. Reject every other prefix, REX, ModR/M/addressing form, VEX/EVEX, truncation, trailing bytes and non-XMM0 form.

Admit only `MXCSR` bits in `0xffbf`, reserved bits clear, all six exception masks set, `DAZ=FTZ=0`. Any RC and all prior IE/DE/ZE/OE/UE/PE stickies are accepted. Unmasked exceptions and `#XM` are not modeled. `AC=1` returns local Unsupported before span validation/read; `AC=0` permits unaligned m64. Check endpoint overflow and canonical48 `[RAX,RAX+7]` before exactly one `read8`. Failed reads preserve the full CPU/SSE/`MXCSR`/RIP state and retirement.

The independent integer `independent_addsd` oracle receives the memory RHS. A halfway fixture poisons `XMM1` and `XMM0.high64`. Direct tests cross four RC modes × 64 sticky histories across midpoint, adjacent, tiny/subnormal, overflow, NaN, infinity and zero cases. Runner matrix asserts `StopAddress`, an available snapshot and retirement count one before oracle validation. Also verify gate/fetch precedence, AC refusal, unaligned read, canonical endpoints, overflow, read rollback, strict schema/provenance, backend denial and S2-37bb register regression.

Validation on the isolated slice passed focused decoder/direct ISA checks 4/4, od-isa 1,795, od-testkit 455, runner 113 unit + 491 fixture tests, and od-x86-runner 8 library + 4 binary tests; its Graphify snapshot had 11,207 nodes / 24,220 edges / 335 communities. Workspace all-target offline check, formatting, layout and Graphify refresh (11,215 nodes / 24,238 edges / 338 communities) also passed. Independent Sol/high review passed. The Linux-only native denial could not run because of the existing ISSUE-029 cross-target blockers; no physical x86 acceptance is claimed. Fragment/C ABI closure follows their separate API/decoder boundaries and has no dedicated S2-37dj negative test. Full details: [standalone report](../reports/S2_37DJ_ADDSD_MEMORY.md).

No physical x86 acceptance is claimed. Sources: Intel SDM Rev. 093 Vol. 2A `ADDSD` pp. 3-22–3-23 and legacy `SSE2` rows in Table 2-27; Vol. 1 §§4.9.1.4–.6, 11.5.2–11.5.3; Vol. 3A Event 19/Table 7-8.
